subject: Prod inference slowdowns — SwiftPay reserved throughput gap
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@swiftpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: SwiftPay SRE <sre@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: sudden latency & errors from reserved pool - prod

Evelyn,

We're seeing an increase in token latency and a ~2.4% error rate on production inference routes served from our reserved capacity (customer account: SwiftPay). Impact started ~08:40 PT and is ongoing. Surface symptoms: higher p95 token latency (1.4s -> 3.8s), occasional 503s on model/gpt-3.8-quant, and queueing at the prefix/cache layer.

Attached is a quick graph from our monitoring (SLO chart). Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing any saturation on dedicated GPU pools or throttles applied to reserved tenants? This is affecting checkout risk for ~3% of transactions.

Quick ask: can you confirm current pool headroom and any fallback behavior in place? We need a short technical explanation to share with our execs.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Ops, SwiftPay

Attachments: swiftpay_slo_graph_20271018.png
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:28:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & errors from reserved pool - prod

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the graph. We're triaging now.

Immediate notes:
- I'm opening an Ops bridge and looping in RTX pool owners.
- Can you confirm the affected model routes and an example request id? That helps us correlate KV cache pressure vs. kernel contention.

I'll come back with headroom numbers and whether any automatic fallbacks triggered. If needed, we can escalate to the dedicated pool capacity team for a rapid burst.

Evelyn Hart
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 10:02:45 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden latency & errors from reserved pool - prod

Evelyn / team — digging into metrics now. Early findings (first 20m):
- Dedicated pool ID: dp-14-west-2 showing average GPU utilization 94% on sequence-heavy traffic (peak concurrent sequences up +47% vs baseline).
- Async queue depth spiked and KV cache hit rate dipped 8% (likely cache thrash).
- We observed multiple model variants falling back to the quantized path which increased CPU-side token assembly latency.

Action items I'm spinning up:
1) Apply an immediate temporary inbound rate cap for non-critical SwiftPay routes (can be bumped up after ops).
2) Request burst activation from Dedicated team for +2 nodes (30m ETA).
3) Dump a KV cache snapshot and upload for SwiftPay to inspect hot prefixes (attaching reference).

Irene — can you confirm whether any reserved-capacity throttle logs show enforced quota reassignments?

-Jonas

Attachments: kv_cache_snapshot_20271018.tar.gz
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 10:34:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & errors from reserved pool - prod

Jonas — confirmed. Our reservation audit shows dp-14-west-2 is at 98% committed for the current hourly window; automatic partitioning tried to shift load but backpressure propagated to the prefix cache layer. No explicit quota revocations for SwiftPay were recorded, but our admission controller did start shedding low-priority requests for some model routes at 09:47 PT.

I'm escalating to Capacity Engineering (cc'ed) to authorize immediate intra-region burst. Also recommending enabling the 'prefix-kv-protect' override for SwiftPay while we stabilize — reduces tail latency at cost of some unit efficiency.

Irene Choi
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency & errors from reserved pool - prod

Alex — quick public-facing summary to share with your execs: we discovered short-term saturation in the dedicated GPU pool (dp-14-west-2) serving your reserved throughput window. Our admission controller began shedding lower-priority routes at 09:47 PT to preserve core SLA traffic. We're authorizing a two-node intra-region burst which should restore headroom in ~30 minutes and have enabled a temporary prefix-protect policy to reduce tail latency.

Next steps we are taking internally:
- +2 node burst (ETA 30m) — Capacity Eng on it.
- Temporary prefix-kv-protect override for SwiftPay (minimizes cache thrash).
- Post-incident audit to recommend longer-term reserved throughput uplift or scheduled auto-burst for your commit window.

I'll monitor and update once latency returns to baseline. If your execs need an immediate bridge, I can set up a 15-min sync with Capacity Eng and SRE.

Evelyn Hart

Subject: Post-incident update: burst complete, follow-up asks

Quick update — burst activated at 11:20 PT (+2 nodes), latency trended back toward baseline by 11:40 PT. Error rate reduced to 0.2%. Actions we completed:
- Kept prefix-kv-protect enabled for the remainder of the peak hour.
- Gathered KV snapshot and unit telemetry (links above).
- Created a short action list for SwiftPay:
  * We recommend a reserved throughput uplift of +25% for your peak commit window (proposal attached).
  * Optionally enable scheduled auto-burst during known high-volume windows (pricing TBD).

Marissa Cole will own the contract/PROC follow-up to scope the uplift and pricing. Evelyn — can you please coordinate a 30-min call with SwiftPay CTO and our Capacity Eng for tomorrow?

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
